The Insurance Company is on Appeal.
The award of the Tribunal made in M.C.O.P.No.570 of 2011 is under challenge.
2. The claimant, who was the injured in a road accident that occurred on 27.02.2011 around 3.00 p.m. sought for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries suffered by her in the said accident.

It was her claim that when she was travelling as a Pillion Rider with her husband in a two wheeler belonging to her husband, bearing Regn. No.TN 29-H- 4079, another two wheeler, bearing Regn. No. TN 29-AD-7986, which was driven by its rider in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the two wheeler, in which, the claimant was riding as a pillion rider, and as a result of which,
the claimant was thrown off from the two wheeler, and she sustained severe head injury and lost her consciousness.

Soon after the accident, she was taken to the Primary Health Care Centre; from there, to the Government Hospital, Papparapatti; then, shifted to Om Sakthi Hospital,
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Dharmapuri and finally, she was taken to Kovai Medical Centre and Hospital, Coimbatore on 28.12.2011, where, she was treated as inpatient nearly for three months.

entities.text: Kovai Medical Centre and Hospital, Coimbatore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Due to severe head injury sustained by the claimant, she remained in a semi conscious state even at the time when the claim petition was filed before the Tribunal.

3. The second respondent/Insurance Company, insurer of the two wheeler, filed a counter statement, inter alia contending that the two wheeler, which was insured with them was not at all involved in the accident.
According to the Insurance Company, it is a case of fixing of Vehicle by the claimant.

It was also pointed out that the Police had filed a Final Report stating that the vehicle,
which was insured with the second respondent/Insurance Company was not involved in the accident and therefore, prayed for dismissal of the Claim Petition.
4. Before the Tribunal, on the side of the claimant, husband of the claimant was examined as P.W.1 and one Doctor, Krishnakumar was examined as P.W.2 and Exs.P.1 to P.8 were marked.
On the side of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis respondent/Insurance Company, two witnesses were examined as R.W.1 and R.W.2 and Exs.
R.1 and R.2 were marked.

Ex.P.1 is First Information Report (F.I.R.), Ex.P.2 is the Discharge Summary issued by Kovai Medical Centre and Hospital,
Coimbatore, Ex.R.1 is the Accident Register maintained by Kovai Medical Centre, Coimbatore and Ex.R.2 is the Final Report filed by Police.

entities.text:
Kovai Medical Centre and Hospital,
Coimbatore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
5. The Tribunal, on the basis of pleadings framed the following issues for consideration, and the translated English version is as under:-
i) Who is cause for the accident?
ii) Are the respondents 1 and 2 are liable to pay compensation to the petitioner?
Iii) Is the claimant is eligible for compensation, if so, the amount of compensation?
6.
The Tribunal, on appreciating the evidence on record, came to the conclusion that since the investigation was not shown to be done properly Final Report cannot be accepted.

On the said findings, the Tribunal held https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis that it was the negligence on the part M/S. Bajaj Allianz General vs Sujatha on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2854241/
2 of the rider of the two wheeler that belonged to the first respondent before the Tribunal that caused the accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. On quantum, the Tribunal considered the evidence on record and calculated that the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.17,55,650/- for the injuries sustained by her since is found to be in a vegetative state.
8. Against the said award, the Insurance Company is on appeal, as stated supra.

9. Mr.J.Michael Visuvasam learned counsel appearing for the appellant/Insurance Company would draw our attention to the contents of Exs.P.1, P.2, R.1 and R.2 to contend that the vehicle belonging to the second respondent insured with the appellant has been fixed in this case only with a view to extort compensation from the Insurance Company.
The learned counsel would contend that though the accident took place on 27.02.2011, Ex.P.1/F.I.R. was lodged only on 07.03.2011, i.e. after a delay https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis of 8 days.

Drawing our attention to the contents of Exs.P.1, P.2,
R.1 and R.2, learned counsel would further contend that there is unimpeachable evidence to show that the accident occurred due to the collision between a two wheeler and a four wheeler.

The learned counsel would also draw our attention to the Final Report filed by the Police, which would clearly exonerate the owner of the alleged offending vehicle, viz., second respondent herein from the offence.

10. On the contrary, Mr.A.Sakthivel, learned counsel appearing for the first respondent/claimant would contend that the Tribunal has analysed the evidence and it is held that since the investigation was not shown to be done in a proper manner, Final report cannot be accepted and rightly belittled the same and no document has been filed by the appellant/Insurance Company, in support of the contents of the Final Report.

Therefore, according to the learned counsel, de hors the final report,
Tribunal had came to the conclusion that it was the two wheeler owned by the second respondent herein and insured with the appellant was cause for the accident.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 11.
We have heard Mr.J.Michael Visuvasam learned counsel appearing for the appellant/Insurance Company and Mr..A.Sakthivel, learned counsel for the first respondent/claimant.
Second respondent, owner of the offending Vehicle, despite service of notice, has not appeared either in person or through the counsel duly instructed.
12. We have considered the rival submissions.

Sympathies apart, if we examine the evidence on record in the case on hand, we will have to answer the question number one to the effect that the two wheeler insured with the appellant was not the cause of the accident.

13. Unimpeachable documentary evidence is available in the form of Exs.P.1, P.2. and R.1. R.2.
Ex

. P.2 is the Discharge Summary issued by Kovai Medical Centre and Hospital, Coimbatore on 20.05.2011, i.e. after the filing of the First Information Report, which would clearly show that the two wheeler was hit by a four wheeler at Papparapatti.

sentences.text:
3 earliest document available reads as follows:-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ''Alleged history of Two wheeler hit by Tata Sumo''.
The contents of these two documents, viz., Ex.P.2/Discharge Summary and Ex.R.1/Accident Register tally.

However, Ex.P.1/FIR is lodged on 07.03.2011, stating that the accident was caused by an unidentified two wheeler and in the FIR, it is stated that the two wheeler belonged to one Jagadesan of Papparapatti.

Though the learned counsel appearing for the first respondent/claimant would attempt to argue that admission was made at Kovai Medical Centre and Hospital, Coimbatore, by the brother of the injured and therefore, injured's husband cannot be made responsible for any discrepancy in the Accident Register/Ex.R.1 his contention is against the contents of FIR, which states that the husband of the injured also accompanied her when the injured was admitted in Kovai Medical Centrre and Hospital, Coimbatore on 28.02.2011.
14.

sentences.text: We are, therefore, unable to accept the aforesaid contention of the learned counsel for the first respondent/claimant.
Unfortunately, the Tribunal has not adverted to the contents of Ex.P.2/Discharge Summary, Ex.R.1/Accident Register and Ex.R.2/Final Report.

Merely because, the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Police are not able to trace the records related to the enquiry conducted, the Tribunal cannot assume that the accident had occurred due to the negligent riding of the two wheeler.

Even according to the earlier documentary evidence available in the form of Accident Register/Ex.R.1 issued by the reputed Hospital, viz., Kovai Medical Centre and Hospital,
Coimbatore, the involvement of four wheeler, viz. Tata Sumo could be clearly seen.

entities.text:
Kovai Medical Centre and Hospital,
Coimbatore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
We are,
therefore, unable to accept the conclusion of the Tribunal that the two wheeler insured with the appellant was involved in the accident.
Under the circumstances since the involvement of the two wheeler insured with the appellant has not been proved, the Claim Petition has to be necessarily dismissed.
15. In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal filed by the appellant/Insurance Company is allowed.
The judgment and decree passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dharmapuri, in M.C.O.P.No.570 of 2011 is set aside.

Since it is stated that the appellant/Insurance Company has deposited 50% of the award amount as per the conditional stay order granted by the Division Bench on 12.03.2021 in C.M.P.No.4668 of 2021, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the same shall be refunded to the appellant/Insurance Company with all accrued interest, if any .
No costs.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
